evals.expected_output: Claude reads the plan file, extracts task description and steps, writes tests first (RED), Codex audits tests, Claude implements (GREEN), refactors (IMPROVE), Codex reviews final implementation.
expectations: Claude reads the plan file at .claude/plan/email-validation.md (Read tool called on the path)
Claude extracts task description and implementation steps from the plan
Claude writes test files BEFORE any production code (RED phase)
Claude runs new tests and verifies they FAIL before implementing
Claude reads tdd-specialist-role.md from the skill directory
Claude calls codex-call.sh for test audit (Phase 3) with test-focused verdict prompt
Claude implements minimal code to make tests pass (GREEN phase)
Claude calls codex-call.sh for implementation review (Phase 6) with 'git diff $START_SHA'
Phase 6 Codex call is a separate codex-call.sh call (not reusing Phase 3 THREAD_ID)
Delivery includes TDD summary with test count, coverage, and RED/GREEN confirmation

evals.prompt: Add a feature that partially exists — extend the existing password validation to also check for special characters.
evals.expected_output: Claude writes tests, discovers they pass unexpectedly in RED, revises tests to properly test new behavior, re-verifies RED.
expectations: Claude writes test files first
Claude runs new tests and detects they pass unexpectedly
Claude flags the tests as wrong (should fail in RED phase)
Claude revises the tests to properly test the NEW behavior
Claude re-runs revised tests and confirms they now FAIL (proper RED)
Claude does NOT proceed to GREEN phase with passing tests

evals.prompt: Add rate limiting to the login endpoint with TDD.
evals.expected_output: Claude detects dirty worktree and stops — asks user to commit or stash before proceeding.
expectations: Claude checks git status for uncommitted changes in Phase 1
Claude detects dirty worktree (uncommitted changes exist)
Claude stops and asks the user to commit or stash changes
Claude does NOT write any test files or production code
Claude does NOT proceed past Phase 1

evals.prompt: Add input sanitization to the comment submission function using TDD.
evals.expected_output: Codex unavailable: Phase 3 test audit degrades gracefully (skipped), but Phase 6 implementation review fails closed (stops).
expectations: Claude writes tests first and verifies RED
Claude runs the codex-call.sh availability check at Phase 3 and notes 'Codex unavailable — test audit skipped'
Claude proceeds to implement despite Codex being unavailable at Phase 3 (graceful degradation)
Claude runs the codex-call.sh availability check again at Phase 6
Claude stops at Phase 6 and tells user Codex is required for final review
Claude does NOT deliver without the Phase 6 Codex review

evals.prompt: [tdd-claude-codex] Review loop stress case: the reviewer still lists one accepted HIGH finding in rounds 1 through 6 and returns a clean round in round 7.
evals.expected_output: Claude fixes and re-reviews every round, continues into round 6 and round 7, and delivers only after the clean round.
expectations: Claude starts a 6th review round instead of stopping after 3 or 5 rounds
Claude never asks the user whether to keep going because of the round count
Delivery reports a clean final round and zero remaining findings

evals.prompt: [tdd-claude-codex] The first review round returns VERDICT: APPROVED with CRITICAL none, HIGH none, MEDIUM none and LOW: one accepted naming issue.
evals.expected_output: Claude treats the LOW-only round like any other round with findings: fixes it and re-reviews.
expectations: Claude fixes the LOW finding instead of delivering or asking the user
Claude runs another review round after the fix
The same handling applies to a round with only HIGH or only MEDIUM findings

evals.prompt: [tdd-claude-codex] The review call times out twice in a row, then a fresh call returns HIGH findings.
evals.expected_output: Claude keeps going past both failed calls, fixes the findings from the call that answers and re-reviews until a round is clean. The failed calls are never treated as approval.
expectations: Claude reads each error and keeps retrying or switches to another independent reviewer, with no retry count
After the fresh call returns findings, Claude fixes them and re-reviews until a round is clean
Claude never treats a failed call as an approval or as a clean round
Claude does not stop after the second failure or ask the user whether to continue

evals.prompt: [tdd-claude-codex] Every review call fails: codex-call.sh reports Codex is not logged in, and reviewer.sh reports the CodeRabbit CLI is not installed.
evals.expected_output: Claude names the blocker it cannot clear itself and labels the work UNREVIEWED.
expectations: Claude tries another independent reviewer before giving up
Claude tells the user the work is UNREVIEWED and names the blocker (missing Codex login, no CodeRabbit CLI)
Claude does not describe the work as approved or reviewed
